plan: This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. If I bid my value ($40), I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, and I pay the second-highest bid, guaranteeing non-negative profit whenever I win. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win against a bid between my true value and my inflated bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Thus, the optimal bid is simply my true value: $40.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding my value ensures: if I win, I pay less than my value (guaranteed non-negative profit), and if I lose, it's because someone valued it more than me, which is efficient. Bidding higher risks negative profit; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $13, so I'll bid $13.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I bid exactly my value ($17), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay that second-highest bid (always less than my value), guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal bid is simply $17.
